title: MetaTwin-Guard v1.0.1: Explainable and Verifiable Digital-Twin Assurance Backend for a Two-Site Cyber Range — Reference Software, Synthetic Benchmark, Colab Notebook and Field Protocol
description:
MetaTwin-Guard is the reference software artifact (Supplementary File S3) accompanying the article An Explainable and Verifiable Digital Twin of a Two-Site Cyber Range for Metaverse Infrastructure Assurance: Software Artifact and Field Protocol. It implements an assurance backend that decides, for every telemetry update, whether the update may change the shared digital-twin state, why it was flagged, and which evidence record supports that decision.

The package implements Ed25519 event authentication (RFC 8032) and SHA-256 payload hashing with per-source hash chaining (FIPS 180-4); an integrity gateway with schema, payload-hash, signature, identifier, sequence and chain checks; an admission-before-state invariant (rejected events never modify the twin) with explicit freshness classes for stale state; seven transparent static operational rules; a median/MAD robust anomaly score whose top-three feature contributions are the exact decomposition of the score; an integrity-aware hybrid decision; and a four-validator, three-of-four quorum-signed, hash-chained evidence ledger, explicitly a single-process emulation rather than a distributed blockchain.

A deterministic synthetic benchmark (master seed 20260823; six scenarios × eight runs; 17,280 events, 1,920 injected) covers WAN failover, VPN degradation, Wi-Fi authentication surge, power transition, post-signature telemetry modification and replay. Both feature-only modes reach F1 = 0 for replay, while the integrity-aware hybrid reaches F1 ≈ 0.90; an executed layer ablation attributes the replay and modification gains entirely to the integrity layer (integrity-only F1 = 1.000); an executed sensitivity analysis confirms that the dispersion floor, not the threshold, prevents the robust score from detecting isolated binary power transitions; the pattern holds across four additional master seeds; and all 48 evidence chains verify.

The deposit contains the Python package (dependency: cryptography), 27 unit and regression tests, run-level and summary CSV/JSON results, figures (360 dpi PNG and SVG), a self-contained Google Colab notebook with step-by-step demonstrations and conclusions, the prospective field-experiment protocol (S1), a blank field-data workbook with data dictionary (S2), and citation metadata linking all DOIs cited in the article.

Evidence boundary: all results are deterministic software-level verification on synthetic data, not cyber-range field measurements. No physical field run or human-participant study has been performed; field performance, distributed-ledger behaviour and benefit to metaverse users remain to be established. The deterministic Ed25519 keys are test fixtures and must never be used in a deployment. The software processes exported or synthetic telemetry only and performs no scanning, exploitation or network reconfiguration.
